vulnerability.name: IAC-013
vulnerability.description: GitHub Action pinned to mutable tag instead of commit SHA

statements.impact_statement: All flagged actions are pinned via dependabot from trusted publishers (actions/, github/, docker/, goreleaser/, golangci/). Each version bump generates a new line-content fingerprint that re-triggers this rule for the same low-actual-risk pattern. Dependabot keeps these up-to-date; the publisher allowlist effectively covers the supply-chain risk this rule targets at the project level.

vulnerability.name: IAC-018
vulnerability.description: Workflow step suppresses failures with continue-on-error

statements.impact_statement: Both continue-on-error uses in .github/workflows/nox-scan.yml are deliberate and scoped to steps that REPORT, never to the gate that decides. The taint-analysis plugin install tolerates a registry 404 because the plugin is an enrichment -- core rules ship in nox itself -- so an outage should cost the taint rules, not the whole scan. The SARIF upload tolerates failure because GitHub code scanning requires Code Security, which private repos without GHAS lack, and returns "Resource not accessible by integration" there even with security-events: write. The gating step ("Gate on net-new critical/high findings") deliberately carries no continue-on-error and no hashFiles guard, so it cannot be skipped into a green result.

vulnerability.name: IAC-153
vulnerability.description: GitHub Actions artifact upload without attestation

statements.impact_statement: The two flagged uploads (.github/workflows/security.yml and .github/workflows/nox-scan.yml) publish scan output -- SARIF, findings.json and the CycloneDX SBOM -- as short-retention CI artefacts (30 and 7 days). They are diagnostic reports read by maintainers in the Actions UI; nothing installs, executes or redistributes them, so there is no downstream consumer for a provenance statement to protect. Adding actions/attest-build-provenance would require granting id-token:write and attestations:write to the two workflows that run on pull_request -- widening the token scope of exactly the jobs that must stay least-privileged -- and the attestation step cannot succeed on fork PRs, where GitHub withholds the OIDC token. Artefacts that ARE distributed (release binaries and the ghcr.io images) are produced by .github/workflows/release.yml via goreleaser, which is the correct place to attach provenance; that is tracked separately from this scan-report gate.

vulnerability.name: DATA-005
vulnerability.description: Hardcoded public IP address in configuration

statements.impact_statement: The address in cmd/chronos/health.go is 127.0.0.1, an IPv4 loopback literal, which is by definition not a public IP. `chronos health` is the container HEALTHCHECK probe: the runtime image is gcr.io/distroless/static, which ships no shell and no curl, so the binary probes its own /health endpoint. Loopback is the only correct dial target -- containerised deployments set CHRONOS_HTTP_HOST=0.0.0.0, a bind wildcard that cannot be dialled -- and a literal avoids depending on name resolution inside a distroless image that ships no resolver configuration. The port is not hardcoded; it is read from CHRONOS_HTTP_PORT via config.Default(), and -addr overrides the whole base URL.

Both continue-on-error uses in .github/workflows/nox-scan.yml are deliberate and scoped to steps that REPORT, never to the gate that decides. The taint-analysis plugin install tolerates a registry 404 because the plugin is an enrichment -- core rules ship in nox itself -- so an outage should cost the taint rules, not the whole scan. The SARIF upload tolerates failure because GitHub code scanning requires Code Security, which private repos without GHAS lack, and returns "Resource not accessible by integration" there even with security-events: write. The gating step ("Gate on net-new critical/high findings") deliberately carries no continue-on-error and no hashFiles guard, so it cannot be skipped into a green result.

test/integration/docker-compose.yml is a local/CI smoke-test harness, not production kustomize. Both services default to :latest so a developer compose-up pulls the current GHCR release; CHRONOS_IMAGE / MNEMOS_IMAGE override the tag for a local build. Changing the registry (felixgeelhaar → klarlabs-studio) re-fingerprints the same :latest line and would otherwise re-fail the unwaived gate on every image-name edit.
